hypothesis: For SOL breakout-onset lifecycles only, a 40-bps favorable-excursion activation followed by a 15-bps floor and 20-bps trailing giveback may reduce late maximum-hold reversals when causal regime structure support has remained at or below 0.25 for five consecutive completed one-minute decisions. The same mechanism is not expected to transfer to HYPE because retrospective HYPE lifecycles show materially larger continuation value.
decision: Keep the authorized v14 runtime, entries, sizing, venue protection, maximum-hold controller, and execution scope unchanged. Reject portfolio-wide or HYPE use of the support-decay profit lock because the retrospective all-live mechanism reduces mean normalized return. Freeze the exact a40_floor15_trail20 policy as a report-only SOL breakout observer beginning at the prospective cutoff. Record every later qualifying activation, theoretical trigger, estimated after-fee and funding result, actual exit, and missed continuation; do not let this observer close, retain, resize, rank, gate, or promote a live position.
falsifier: The SOL-specific hypothesis is weakened if prospective SOL breakout lifecycles show the frozen observer reducing after-cost return, triggering before profitable continuation, or failing to improve peak-giveback capture. It is strengthened only provisionally if independent later SOL lifecycles improve after actual fees, funding, slippage, and gap-through assumptions without relying on one side or one market episode. Any changed threshold, persistence, activation, floor, trail, bar timing, or cost class is a new trial and cannot be pooled with this frozen observer.
limitations: The SOL policy was selected after inspecting one completed SOL loss and is hypothesis-formation evidence, not validation.
The one SOL lifecycle is a short and cannot establish repeatability, long-side behavior, or regime stability.
The portfolio-wide and HYPE retrospective results are materially worse than actual exits, so the observer must remain SOL-provider-specific.
Completed one-minute bars cannot prove intrabar ordering, private queue position, or the exact fill available at a theoretical stop trigger.
Estimated exits apply observed exit fee rate and reference-to-fill ratio, but future gap-through and latency may be worse.
The all-live comparison combines multiple historical profiles and is normalized mechanism evidence rather than deployable portfolio PnL.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, target, sizing policy, backend process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
